title: What are the rules for cooking in camping? May I use a stove to cook?
content: The use of outdoor cooking appliances is permitted in the Car Camping, Ready-Set camping & La Campana camping. Cooking is not allowed in Lake Eldorado spots, though there is a communal Lake Eldorado cooking area. The following is a list of the requirements for approval of outdoor cooking appliances: All cooking appliances shall bear a certification or listing from a nationally recognized test or certification organization. Cooking within the interior of a vehicle/tent is prohibited. All cooking appliances shall not exceed 2 burners per cooking appliance. All cooking appliances shall be classified as a table top device and shall be placed on a flat level surface (no standalone cooking devices). A minimum of 3 feet of clearance shall be maintained at all times while cooking appliance is in use. No combustible material shall be within 3 feet of the cooking appliance. Cooking appliance that only utilizes propane as the fuel source shall be permitted. No wood, charcoal, butane, flammable/combustible liquid cooking appliances or items permitted. One cooking appliance per camp site shall be permitted Maximum amount of propane per campsite shall not exceed 20 pounds or 48 pounds of water capacity or 4.7 gallons of propane OR 6 -1-pound propane disposable cylinders Cooking appliances shall only be used during the hours of 7:00am to 2:00 am (PST) Cooking appliances, when in use, shall not be left unattended. View Permitted/Not Permitted car camping grill examples here . More information and Not Allowed list can be found on the camping page .

title: Camping: What defines a legal guardian?
content: A legal guardian is a person who has the legal authority and corresponding duty to care for the personal and property interests of another person, called a ward. Usually, a person has the status of guardian because the ward is incapable of caring for his or her own interests due to infancy, incapacity, or disability. Most countries and states have laws that provide that the parents of a minor child are the legal guardians of that child, and that the parents can designate who shall become the child’s legal guardian in the event of death. A legal guardianship is obtained through court order, and the legal process for doing so is initiated by the prospective guardian. Please note: An older sibling, older friend or friend of the family does not automatically count as a legal guardian. A legal guardian is someone who would be held legally responsible for you by a court of law. Generally, a legal guardian is the one who takes care of the minor when the minor’s birth-parents are no longer living, in jail or have lost their legal rights. title: Health & Safety: CODE OF CONDUCT
content: Coachella Art and Music Festival is committed to creating a safe, comfortable, and family-friendly experience for our guests. The following actions may result in ejection from the event: Profanity or other offensive language, whether spoken or appearing on apparel or memorabilia Intoxication and/or signs of impairment related to excessive alcohol consumption Bringing prohibited items into festival grounds (venue and/or camping) Throwing of items or liquids Taunting, abusive, or disruptive language and obscene or offensive gestures, imagery, or symbolism Entering the stage or accessing seated/restricted areas at any time without proper passes Public nudity/indecency, including urinating in public (anywhere other than the proper restroom) Engaging in sexual behavior in public Possession/use/sale of illegal drugs Fighting or other threatening behavior that may harm, endanger, threaten, or bring discomfort to anyone Damage, destruction, vandalism, or theft of any property Fraudulently claiming a disability or abuse of Accessibility (ADA) services Sitting/Standing/Loitering in designated Fire Lanes and Pedestrian walkways Violation of state or local laws Festival and Event Management reserves the right to enforce these policies at their discretion. The vehicle will be removed from the property. Offenders may be arrested. No refund will be issued if ejected.

title: Groop Leader
content: Groop Leader registration is opens Friday, December 5th at 10am CT! You can sign up Friday and start organizing your Groop. Groop Leader Registration Deadline is April 3rd, 2026 . Groop Camping gives you and your friends the option of arriving at separate times and having a campsite set aside for you no matter when you arrive so you can all camp together. You must have a minimum of 24 people to create a Groop and you will receive 1 parking pass per 3 people in your Groop (i.e. a Groop of 24 people will receive 8 parking passes total), so carpooling is a must. The Groop Leader will determine which individuals in the Groop will receive parking passes and will be responsible for submitting mailing addresses for all recipients after the Groopie registration has passed in May. The bigger the Groop the more space you’ll receive and the more parking passes you’ll receive. We are not able to allocate additional parking passes so please plan accordingly. After adding your Groop Leader Pass to your cart, you’ll be able to create your Groop’s camp name directly on the checkout screen. Feel free to make these as fun as you want! title: What should I pack? (packing list)
content: Prepare thyself! Need some pointers on how to impROOve your camping experience? Check out our list of packing suggestions! DON’T LEAVE HOME WITHOUT IT 🚫 Camping gear (Tents & Shelters, Sleeping Bags & Beds, Tarp) A shade structure is a big help in the campsite! Cooler and/or water jugs to refill (ice available for purchase throughout the campgrounds) Lantern / flashlight / headlamp (AND extra batteries!) Reusable water bottle (or two!) Camping chairs, tables, and anything else that might help create a comfy home-away- from home Rain gear (failure to bring it increases the chance of rain) Your favorite hoodie (yes, it CAN get cold in TN) Extra shoes/sneakers (treat yo feet!) Mud boots (in case it rains) Bug spray (we recommend without DEET – be green!) Sunscreen (lots of it) A hat for shade A bandana (in Tennessee, in June, you’re going to sweat) Sunglasses Biodegradable plastic bags for trash (we do provide some bags for trash and recycling, but extras are nice) Toilet paper (we provide plenty, but some backup is always a good idea) Flag or balloon to identify your campsite Extra set of keys to keep with you at all times (avoid keeping keys in your car!) YOU DON’T NEED IT TO SURVIVE, BUT HAPPY YOU HAVE IT 😎 Small stove or grill if you would like to cook some of your own food (please obey our Gasoline/Charcoal/Propane Policy ) Small luggage lock for your tent (please don’t bring any valuables – if you must, keep them locked out of view in your vehicle) or rent one of our lockers Vehicle key code (this makes it easy for the locksmith to duplicate your car key if you lose it) Phosphate-free and sulfate-free soaps, detergents and shampoos Smokers – bring an ashtray! Every butt you throw on the ground, someone has to pick up! Blanket (for sitting) Earplugs (for sleeping) Portable speakers or radio

title: What items are allowed and prohibited?
content: Each person, their belongings, and their vehicle are subject to search upon entry. Please view the list below to see what you can and cannot bring in specific to different areas of the festival. Note that the list is different in the campgrounds and Centeroo (generally speaking, you can bring many things into the campgrounds, but fewer items into Centeroo).

title: CAMPGROUNDS/OUTEROO
content: The following items are ALLOWED : ALL vehicles will be searched before entry. Alcohol 2-cases of beer per person, 2-boxes of wine per person per car and 1-1.75 liter of hard liquor per person per car. Food / drinks Point and shoot cameras / cameras with detachable lens less than 2” long Portable camping grill Forty (40) pounds of charcoal per grill per vehicle will be allowed. If you aren't bringing in a grill... then you won't be allowed any charcoal. Propane tanks 20lbs or smaller will be allowed. Only 1 propane tank per grill per vehicle or 2 small "Coleman" type tanks per grill per vehicle. Generator (smaller than 4KW) 1 generator per vehicle. No more than 10 gallons of gasoline in an appropriate container per generator per vehicle will be allowed. Any amount greater than that will be confiscated. If you aren't bringing in a generator you won't be allowed to bring any gas. Instruments (but please be mindful of your neighbors). Camping Tools (Tent mallets, tent anchors, knives no longer than palm length for cooking purposes) Hand Tools (allowed at security's discretion) Factory sealed Naloxone /Narcan kit The following items are PROHIBITED : ALL vehicles will be searched before entry. Glass Wooded Fires Kegs Weapons Drones Fireworks Illegal Substances Bicycles or any other wheeled transportation devices Professional cameras (with detachable lenses longer than 2” long) Pets (except service animals) Glow sticks Box trucks / tractor-trailers Laser pens or similar focused light device Vending (sharing, yes. Selling, no) Power Tools or Tools with gas motors

title: What are the rules for each camping and parking pass type?
content: Every person needs a Centeroo Ticket to be at Bonnaroo and every car, truck, SUV, minivan or other standard vehicle will need a camping or parking pass in order to enter Bonnaroo (think of it like a ticket for your car). All camping passes are per vehicle, not per person. So, for example, multiple individuals can camp together in one campsite with just one car camping pass (as long as they each have a Centeroo Ticket). Primitive Car Camping Pass Primitive Car Camping is the classic, most affordable way to camp at Bonnaroo. Campsite sizes are roughly 20’x20’ (including the space for your car). You may NOT buy extra campsites around a single vehicle – you will get as many spots as you have cars AND passes together. There is no “per person” camping fee. So if, for example, you have 3 people coming in one car, you only need 1 Primitive Car Camping Pass (everyone will need a Centeroo Ticket though). Primitive Car Camping passes have assigned entry days. You will need to purchase the pass that corresponds with the day you plan on arriving (Either Wednesday or Thursday). If you have purchased into one of our specialty programs like RV Camping, Glamping, Groop Camping, or Community Camping, then you will need a program specific vehicle pass (usually included in your order for that program) and won’t need a normal Primitive Car Camping Pass. Carpool Car Camping Pass The Carpool Primitive Camping pass is basically the same as the classic Primitive Car Camping pass with one difference. This pass is for groups with 3+ Bonnaroovians arriving in the same vehicle together ONLY. It's simple - help save the planet and save money at the same time! If you arrive with a Carpool Primitive Camping pass and less than 3 people in your vehicle, you will be required to purchase a primitive car camping pass at the tollbooth. RV Camping Passes An RV pass is required for each RV entering the campgrounds (think of it like a wristband for your RV). Each RV space will be about 20′ x 50′. Tents can be set up if they are within this space, and any shade structures or awnings must fit within this designated space too. The following vehicles are considered an RV, and every RV entering The Farm requires an RV Pass: Any size RV: Class A, Class B or Class C Any size bus (no tour buses, prevosts, or motorcoaches with low clearance allowed) Any vehicle wider or longer than a normal 15 passenger van (230.8″ x 79.3″ x 82.3″) Any vehicle towing a camper or 5th wheel of any size. If you’re hitching anything, it’s an RV. (Box trucks and trailers are not allowed into the campgrounds.) Find more information about RV rules and requirements. Need a companion vehicle? Read more about companion passes for RVs. Pre-Pitched Tents & Glamping Options Leave the tent pitching and furnishing to us and camp in style with these enhanced options! Each rental is pre-pitched and comes with a vehicle pass that gets you parked in a special lot just a short walk from the rented camping accommodation (but note that your car will not be parked immediately next to your tent). Need a companion vehicle? Read more about companion passes for pre-pitched accommodations . Day Parking Pass Not camping? No problem! The Day Parking Pass is for you. This pass grants one daily parking spot in the Cosmic Nomads “Day Parking Lot”. Passes are good for the day you choose at checkout, and allow you to park for the duration of all performances on the purchased day. The Day Parking Lot opens at 11am each day and will close at 6am the following day. Vehicles still in the lot at 9am the day after your pass is valid for are subject to tow. Vehicles larger than a standard 15-passenger van are not allowed and you MAY NOT SLEEP IN YOUR VEHICLE. To keep in mind: There are no in and out privileges for day parking passes. Passes are good for one entry on the day they are designated for.

title: Can I use rideshares or get dropped off at Bonnaroo?
content: While getting to Bonnaroo with ride-shares is totally possible, it’s not the most convenient way to do things. Manchester is a very small town, which causes two complications: Lots of traffic on the small-town roads Very few rideshare cars available nearby. It also could take hours based on incoming/outgoing traffic for rideshare drivers to reach a tollbooth. Because we prioritize the traffic flow for campers (the vast majority of the traffic), there is no “priority lane” of any kind for rideshares either, which can mean long lines at certain times. With all this in mind, you will be much happier scheduling a ride ahead of time and/or renting a car if possible. If you do choose to get to the Farm using rideshares or are getting dropped off, use this address, 2465 Ne w Bushy Branch Rd, Manchester, TN 37355 , to be directed to the East Tollbooth.

title: Arrival Pro-Tips & Advice
content: Arrival Pro-Tips Like officers everywhere, Tennessee police expect you to obey the highway safety laws, and they’re prepared to enforce them. They’re especially strict about open container violations, so think, do you really want to start the weekend in the slammer? Law enforcement is looking out for your safety and want you to have a good time. Tell them thank you and trust that they want to get you onto the Farm more than anyone. Please stay in your car, especially when you’re waiting in line to enter the festival. This is no time for hacky sack. Bonnaroo is a friendly place. Don’t kill the vibe by cutting in line. You’ll be in soon, we promise. How to deal with the inevitable traffic delays: Fill up your tank before getting in line to enter the festival. There are no gas stations on-site. We suggest stopping and filling up when you’re still an hour or so away – things will get more crowded as you get closer. Empty YOUR tank, too, before you arrive. There are no bathrooms in line. Pack some snacks and nonalcoholic beverages (remember, arrival tip #1). Play 20 Questions.

title: Health, Safety & Security
content: SAFETY AND SECURITY The safety and well-being of our fans, artists, guests and staff is paramount. Organizers work closely with local officials to ensure the safest possible experience. You’ll notice uniformed security throughout the festival grounds. They are there to keep you safe, so don’t hesitate to ask them for help if you need immediate assistance. REMEMBER: You’re the eyes and ears of the festival. If you see something suspicious, say something. ENTRY PROTOCOLS For the safety of everyone entering the festival, all fans are subject to a full and complete airport-style search prior to entry. This may include a full body pat-down and magnetometer screening before entry. If you would like to be screened by security personnel of your same gender, please let security personnel know prior to the search process. Screening of children will always take place with the consent of a parent or guardian. Please review our Allowed and Prohibited items list before heading to the festival. COME PREPARED & LOOK OUT FOR EACH OTHER Here are four easy ways to look out for yourself and those around you: Watch out for your neighbors – if someone around you looks like they need help, check in with them. If someone is getting unruly, alert the nearest staff member. Keep an eye on your belongings. Be considerate – this is a shared space and we want everyone to enjoy themselves. title: Staying Comfortable - Tips from Experienced Bonnaroovians
content: Four days of camping in Tennessee is no simple task. Add in a few hundred musical acts and more than a few thousand new friends and it gets even more complicated. Here are some tips to keep yourself comfy and healthy while at Bonnaroo. It's a marathon, not a sprint It's a cliche, we know. But seriously, no human being can go at 100% for all of Bonnaroo. That's not a challenge, it's just a fact. Plan rest breaks during the day, stay hydrated and well fed, and be honest with yourself if/when you're not feeling well. We all hate to admit it, but sometimes you gotta miss one set to make it to a bunch more. Listen to your body! Refill your water often, and keep stocked on ice There are water stations throughout the festival for a reason. Keep those water bottles filled, and keep yourself hydrated. Also be sure to pick up some extra ice from the vendors in the campgrounds each morning to keep your food and drinks cold at the campsite. Some folks like to freeze some water bottles before they leave for the farm. That way you have ice for a day or two, then a drink after that! Eat Smart If you were about to run a 10k, you'd eat more than some Cheetos and Kool-aid, right? Same goes for Bonnaroo. Make sure you bring some healthy snacks to keep you energized throughout the day, and visit our food vendors for some hearty meals too. Dancing and partying take a lot of energy - make sure you have what you need! Ask for help if you need it! Not feeling well? Don't be afraid to ask our staff or SafeFest team for directions to the nearest medical tent. The Bonnaroo team (and other Bonnaroovians too) are always happy to help, but we aren't mind readers (yet) so don't be afraid to ask for support if you need it. No need to "rough it": showers, water, and bathrooms are your friends There are showers at most plazas that you can use for a small fee, as well as nicer trailer bathrooms and water stations around the campgrounds (you'll likely be closer to a porta-potty, but sometimes the extra walk is worth the effort). Take some time to take care of yourself. Brush your teeth, drink your water, and do all those other things your mom would be saying if she were here. You'll feel better and you'll be better prepared to take on the day. Extra batteries and chargers for your phone are great to have Nobody wants to run the car engine just to charge their phone - plus the exhaust from the car can be a serious carbon monoxide hazard (be careful!). If you have one, bringing a battery to charge your phone every once and a while will help keep you comfortable. Shade & airflow make all the difference : When planning your campsite, keep in mind that you will be in an open grassy field in Tennessee. It's gonna get hot, and you won't want to be in direct sunlight when chilling at your campsite. Bring a shade canopy to cover your area, and even consider another to add more shade on top of your tent. No Bonnaroovian has ever said "we have too much shade at this campsite". Many Bonnaroovians hang cloth tapestries from the edge of their shade tents too, which help block the sun at lower angles but also wont block too much airflow. Also, be wary of tightly enclosed spaces (like the inside of a zipped-up tent). They are great to keep warm at night, but when the sun is out, they will become a greenhouse, and you won't want to be inside of them for any longer than you have to be. Consider a smaller tent to sleep inside of to maximize the shaded area outside your tent during the day. Some people even simply set up a sleeping cot under a shade canopy and call it a day (though do be sure to have a plan for rain if this is the way you choose to go).

This will be enforced by Las Vegas Metro PD and the Nevada Highway Patrol.

title: Charter Buses
content: Private charter buses will NOT have access to the Speedway during EDC Las Vegas. We highly recommend using the Official EDC Shuttle Service to ensure your ride to the festival site.

title: Shuttle FAQ: What Standard Shuttle stop locations can I choose from? Can I ride from any Standard Shuttle stop with my Standard pass?
content: Each Standard Shuttle pass is only valid for a specific location. You cannot use your pass at any other stop. The Standard Shuttle stop locations are: World Market Center: 435 S Grand Central Pkwy The Rio: 3700 W Flamingo Road The Strat: 2000 S Las Vegas Blvd MidStrip: 3645 S Las Vegas Blvd

title: Shuttle FAQ: How often will the Standard Shuttles run?
content: Standard Shuttles will depart continuously from 6:30pm–11:00pm. Return service from EDC back to your stop will begin at 2:00 am and conclude 60 minutes after the music ends at Kinetic Field. Shuttles do not run from 11:00 pm to 2:00 am.

title: Shuttle FAQ: What Premier Shuttle stop locations can I choose from?
content: The Premier Shuttle stop locations are: Virgin Hotels Las Vegas: 4455 Paradise Rd The Strat: 2000 S Las Vegas Blvd World Market Center: 435 S Grand Central Pkwy The Rio: 3700 W Flamingo Road MidStrip: 3645 S Las Vegas Blvd

title: Shuttle FAQ: What time will the Premier Shuttles run?
content: At checkout, you will have the option to reserve the following Premier Shuttle departure and return times (availability permitting). Please note, your departure and return time will be the same for all three days of EDC: Premier Departures: 6:30 pm, 8:30 pm, 10:30 pm Premier Returns: 3:00am, 4:30am, 6:00am Shuttles do not run from 11:00 pm - 2:00 am.

title: Shuttle FAQ: If I have a Premier Shuttle Pass, can I ride the shuttle at any time, leaving from any stop?
content: Each Premier Shuttle Pass is valid for a specific Premier Shuttle stop at a reserved time and cannot be used at any other Premier stop or at an alternate time. If you miss your reserved time we will honor your pass within your stop's standard service. All shuttle passes are valid for the stop designated at purchase only.

title: Shuttle FAQ: Will there be a fast-pass lane for GA+ and VIP ticket holders at the standard shuttle stops?
content: Standard EDC Shuttle stops will have a fast-pass lane through security on the inbound trip for GA+ ticket holders and VIP ticket holders, but this fast-pass does not prioritize VIP or GA+ passes once past the security checkpoint.

title: Shuttle FAQ: Can I purchase an official shuttle pass from anywhere other than this website?
content: The only place to purchase an official EDC Las Vegas Shuttle pass is through the official EDC Las Vegas website with our official ticketing partner Front Gate Tickets. Note: This is the official Shuttle Program of EDC Las Vegas, and we do not oversee any independently offered shuttle programs. Only the official EDC Shuttles will have access to the Speedway and optimized routes to get you there even faster. Third-party services are not endorsed and will not have access to the event grounds.

title: Shuttle FAQ: Can I ride the shuttles to the Opening Ceremonies?
content: Yes! The Cosmic MEADOW gates will open at 5pm on Friday ONLY, followed by a pre-party & Opening Ceremonies from 5pm–7pm. All shuttle pass holders looking to attend the Opening Ceremonies can RSVP for early shuttles leaving from The Rio (running continuously from 4pm–6:00pm) for the additional cost of $20. All Shuttle Pass holders, regardless of shuttle location, are able to add this option, but you must go to The Rio to catch the Opening Ceremony shuttle. Please note: Opening Ceremony passes are limited and may sell out.

title: Shuttle FAQ: Are the shuttles wheelchair-accessible?
content: Yes, we do have wheelchair-accessible shuttles. So that we can best accommodate you, please reach out to the EDC Las Vegas Shuttle Support Team at least two weeks prior to the festival via our contact form or 888-334-4496 with your order number, shuttle stop, phone number, and departure time

title: Shuttle FAQ: How long will it take to get to the festival?
content: We cannot accurately predict the exact traffic on the day of the festival, but our experienced team will have thoroughly vetted routes and do everything in their power to circumnavigate festival traffic to get you to the party as quickly as possible!

title: Shuttle FAQ: Is it possible to change the time or location of my shuttle pass?
content: While we can’t make any promises, you can reach out to the EDC Las Vegas Shuttle Support Team through our contact form or 888-334-4496 , and they can look into your options. Please have ready your order number, shuttle stop, and desired shuttle stop—and/or time slot purchased and desired time, if you have a Premier Pass.

title: Shuttle FAQ: How will I know what shuttle to take at the end of the night?
content: All shuttles will be clearly labeled, and EDC Las Vegas Shuttle Support Team members will be available to direct you to the correct loading area.

title: Shuttle FAQ: If I lose my shuttle pass, can I get it reissued?
content: Once you receive your shuttle pass in the mail, please keep it safe. If you lose your shuttle pass, please visit one of our box offices at your specific shuttle departure location. We will be able to void your original pass and issue a new one for a $20 replacement fee , as long as you present proper photo identification and the credit card used to purchase. Please note: We can replace shuttle passes only once. If you lose your shuttle pass twice, we will not be able to reissue it a second time.

title: Shuttle FAQ: Can I buy a shuttle pass at one of the shuttle stops or on-site at the festival?
content: Our shuttle passes will most likely be sold out by the time of the event. We encourage you to purchase your passes early.

title: Shuttle FAQ: Will there be restrooms on the shuttles?
content: While we are unable to guarantee restrooms on every shuttle, there will be restrooms at all shuttle stops and upon arrival at EDC.

title: Shuttle FAQ: Are there items I am not allowed to bring onto the shuttles?
content: There will be a security pre-check at all shuttle stops, and any items that are prohibited inside the festival are prohibited on the shuttles, including outside food and drink. Be sure to thoroughly review the list of acceptable and prohibited items .

title: Shuttle FAQ: I don’t need my shuttle pass anymore. Can my friend use it?
content: It is perfectly fine to give your shuttle pass to a friend. However, if they lose it, they will need a photocopy of your ID and credit card used to purchase in order to have the pass reissued for the $20 replacement fee. We recommend you give this information to them in advance.

title: Shuttle FAQ: Can I use my EDC Las Vegas Shuttle purchase for a contest/giveaway or to promote my website/product/event?
content: No. EDC Las Vegas trademarks, intellectual property, tickets, and other offerings may NOT be used for advertising, promotions, auctions, contests, sweepstakes, or any commercial purpose, without express written consent from EDC and its partners.

title: Alcohol
content: You must be 21+ to consume alcohol in the campground. If entering with alcohol, you must present government-issued identification. Law enforcement will frequent the campground and randomly card campers seen drinking alcohol. Underage drinkers risk receiving a citation or even being arrested. 21+ campers are advised to carry their government-issued identification AT ALL TIMES. Prohibited: Liquor above 16% ABV or glass of any kind. Acceptable: Beer and alcoholic drinks under 16% ABV, up to 24 cans per person (under 12oz), or up to 5L of wine.

title: Safety
content: For your safety, sleeping in parked vehicles is prohibited, with the exception of RV camping. The campground will be fully staffed by our Ground Control team, as well as medical and security personnel, 24 hours a day. We will also offer shade structures, free filtered drinking water refill stations, and water misters to help keep you cool during the day. Please take care of your valuables. Neither Insomniac nor the venue is responsible for any lost or stolen items.

title: Item Lists
content: Note: Camp EDC Acceptable/Prohibited item lists differ from those of the general festival. Read below for camping guidelines, or view the festival guidelines .

title: Essential Packing List
content: We highly recommend bringing the following items for the most comfortable camping experience. Remember: It’s only four days! Roll your clothes, and pack lightly. YES 2 travel-size locks for your tent YES Bicycles—don’t forget your bike lock! (Only 1 bike per person. Bring at your own risk. Bicycles left in unauthorized areas or fire lanes will be removed.) YES Earplugs YES Eye masks YES Flags/banners/totems to distinguish your tent (see guidelines ) YES Folding chairs YES Food and beverages/water YES Ice chest/coolers YES Phone charger YES Reusable, official Insomniac water bottles YES Sleeping bags, blankets, pillows, air mattress (Note: these items are provided with a Desert Rose camping pass). YES Sunglasses, hats, and sunscreen YES Towels and sandals (for use in the shower) YES Trash bags

title: Acceptable Items
content: These additional items are encouraged at Camp EDC: YES Bicycles (Must be wearing helmet) YES Flags/banners/totems to distinguish your tent (see Totem Guidelines) YES Hydration packs with no more than two main compartments and one smaller compartment (must be empty upon entry) including 2.5L Hydration Packs YES Non-professional flash/still cameras and hand-held video cameras (e.g., Sony Action Cam, GoPro, Polaroids) YES Personal-size battery-powered speakers YES Personal-size pool floaties (made for no more than one adult) YES Physician-prescribed medication that is not expired (must show physician’s prescription and consult with a safety officer upon entry) YES Plastic stakes and rubber mallets YES Small, portable propane grills/stoves with small tanks, up to 4 lbs per group (propane bottles that are part of your RV/camping trailer’s internal system are OK, even if they exceed 4 lbs) YES Sunscreen lotion (inspected upon entry) YES Tampons and pads (must be sealed at entry) YES Wagons (must be soft-sided, collapsible) YES Food (not in glass containers) YES Water * Only you can prevent campground fires! During your stay in the campground, please monitor all cooking devices while in use, and turn off tanks when you’re finished. If you see an unattended fire, please notify a campground staff member immediately.

title: Prohibited Items
content: The following are NOT allowed at Camp EDC: NO Aerosol products/cans NO Laser pointers NO Air horns NO Liquor above 16% ABV or glass of any kind. NO Butane grills or accessories, such as torches NO Costumes that resemble public safety uniforms (police, SWAT, fire, security, medical, life guards) in any way NO Camping wind turbines NO Dollies or hand trucks NO Drones or remote-control aircraft NO Drugs or illegal substances NO Dry ice NO Fireworks NO Gas generators (solar-powered generators OK) NO Glass (small bottles of perfume/cologne OK) NO Helium balloons NO Hammocks NO Hookahs NO Large speaker systems (Sound systems are limited to USB-powered/personal portable speakers. No amplified sound systems are allowed) NO Loose pills without a prescription, or expired medications of any kind (all medications, prescription or otherwise, must be in their original container) NO Scooters, skateboards, longboards NO Metal stakes & hammers NO Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) canisters or nitrous of any kind NO Open campfires or fires/flames of any kind (propane grills OK) NO Personal gas tanks for refueling RVs NO Pets (except service animals) NO Professional recording equipment—photo, video or audio (detachable lenses, tripods, big zooms, or commercial-use rigs) NO Promotional flyers & stickers, promotional/corporate branded banners, or vehicles displaying sponsorships or ads NO Red-colored light-up wands, batons, or lightsabers NO Solar camping showers NO Spray paint NO Weapon or weapon accessories of any kind, real or fictional (including whips, lightsabers, pocket knives, pepper spray, fireworks, fake weapons/props, etc.) NO Unauthorized vending of food or merchandise, including alcohol

title: Accessible Camping
content: Accessible camping locations are available for all tiers of camping for those with accessibility needs! Campsites include close access to paths, entrances, exits, shuttles, accessible restrooms, and accessible showers. Accessible camping spots are available on a first come, first serve basis. Registering helps us prepare for your group and plan our accessible camping locations. Limited spots may be available to unregistered guests onsite, but are not guaranteed . Our encouraged ADA camping registration deadline is April 19th, 2025 to ensure we account for enough ShiftPods and RV spaces allocated in ADA camping locations for all of our ADA campers in need. Registering after this date does not guarantee you will have an allocated ShiftPod or RV space in ADA camping, but we will do our best to accommodate. To register for an ADA camping spot, please fill out our ADA Camping Registration Form . To learn more about the accessible features of Camp EDC, visit our Camp EDC Accessibility Guide . To learn more about the accessible features of the festival grounds, visit our Event Accessibility page. You will need a verified handicap placard or license plate to camp in ADA camping. The person to whom the placard or plate is issued must be present in the vehicle, as a driver or passenger. As part of gaining access to accessible camping, identification will be checked to ensure legitimate use.

title: Tent Camping
content: A $250 damage deposit is required for each ShiftPod booked. One person from each ShiftPod camping group must provide a credit card, upon which a temporary hold will be placed until the ShiftPod and equipment are inspected upon checkout. You are responsible for any and all damages to the ShiftPod and equipment while in your possession and any repair costs and/or excessive cleaning costs incurred as a result of your use of the ShiftPod and equipment. Each campsite will feature a power strip in which to plug in electronic devices. Charging stations are also provided in the Mesa, as well as near the shower compounds. Each tent will be provided with enough power to sustain operation for the power strip. Unplugging the power strip and connecting an external item runs the risk of overloading the circuit, posing a safety hazard to the rest of the campground. If a guest unplugs the power strip, camping personnel reserve the right to unplug the tent from the power grid for the remainder of the festival. This is for the safety and comfort of all guests of Camp EDC.

title: RV Camping
content: Power Add-On required for Dusk Till Dawn RV Passes RVs may not be dropped off, picked up, or set by a third party, or by anyone who does not have a valid festival ticket and camping pass. Each camper must have a valid festival ticket and camping pass and must arrive ready in their RV. RVs must be Class A, B or C, ranging from 19′ to 45′. Truck campers and fifth wheels are allowed, as long as they have a separate on-board generator (or purchase a power add-on ), along with an air conditioner unit that doesn’t require the vehicle to be on to operate. No refueling service will be available, so campers are advised to use their accommodations accordingly. You may not exceed the total permitted length of 45 feet, including tow vehicle if applicable. Tow vehicles must remain attached to pull-trailer at all times. If your group is in need of an additional parking pass because you will have an additional vehicle, you will need to park separately in the Turquoise Lot, our designated Camper Parking. Please follow directions from staff. All RVs must have a working air conditioner powered by an on-board generator—the vehicle engine may NOT be left running. All RV guests must arrive to the campground with a full tank of fuel to prevent issues with air conditioning. No personal generator refueling will be permitted. If you have opted to purchase power, you must bring a 75-foot cable with the proper connector. If you are connected to a 30A or 50A power supply, and your RV overloads the power source, tripping the fuse, the breaker will be reset and you will be issued a one-time warning. If it occurs a second time, your RV will be disconnected from the power grid, without a refund, for the remainder of the festival. Once parked, RVs may not be moved until 8am on Monday, May 17th for Dusk Campers or Monday, May 24th for Dawn & Dusk Till Dawn Campers, unless leaving the festival and not returning. If you would like to leave the campsite before the end of the weekend, please reach out to a Camp EDC staff member for an escort.

title: Code of Conduct
content: Campers are expected to be courteous to one another, as well as to event staff. Camp EDC is shared space, and these are your neighbors for the next few days! Please do your part in making this an incredible weekend for everyone. If a guest participating in any of the following behavior is uncooperative or a persistent offender, they will be removed from the festival site. In certain situations, the offender may be arrested. By entering the campground, you agree to adhere to the following code of conduct: All campers must be 18 or older, verified by government-issued ID. All campers must have a festival ticket. All campers must wear their Camp EDC wristband (acquired at check-in). Campers consuming alcohol must be 21 or older, verified by valid photo ID, which may be randomly checked at any time. No vehicle movement will be permitted once parked. Prohibited items confiscated at entry or during the event will NOT be returned. Please don’t bring prohibited items! The following actions may result in a WARNING and/or EJECTION from the campground: Irresponsible use of alcohol Public nudity or lewd behavior Accessing restricted areas without proper passes Taunting, bullying, abusive/disruptive language, and/or obscene gestures Littering Failing to cooperate/comply with campground safety officers Moving RV or vehicle to another location after placement by festival staff Parking or extending any part of RV or tent into fire lanes or outside designated/marked area Violating the tent and RV camping power grid policies The following actions will result in IMMEDIATE EJECTION: Relieving your bladder or bowels anywhere other than approved restrooms/porta-potties Fighting or engaging in any action that may harm, endanger, threaten or bring discomfort to anyone Public sexual behavior Possession/use of illegal drugs Damage, destruction, vandalism or theft of any property

title: Weather
content: The festival will take place rain or shine. Please keep up-to-date on weather reports and plan your attire and preparations accordingly.

title: Zero Tolerance

title: Security & Entry

content: Maximum height is 10 feet. Totems must be made from a lightweight material (e.g., foam, PVC / no solid metal). title: Festival FAQ: What is the DUSK TILL DAWN 12-day experience?
content: This range of dates represents both EDC Week and the EDC Dusk and EDC Dawn weekends. We have a lot planned for the week in between, stay tuned!

title: Festival FAQ: Is the production and the experience the same between EDC Dusk and EDC Dawn?
content: Yes! The experience and production will maintain the same quality across both weekends.

title: Festival FAQ: What time does the event start & end each day?
content: Friday, May 14, Saturday, May 15, Sunday, May 16, Friday, May 21, Saturday, May 22 & Sunday, May 23: full grounds open 7:00pm–5:30am. Opening ceremony takes place at Cosmic Meadow on Friday, May 14 and Friday, May 21 beginning at 5:00pm.

title: Festival FAQ: Can I enter anytime?
content: As long as you are holding a valid ticket that has not yet been scanned, you may enter until an hour before the end of the event. Ins & outs are not allowed.

title: Festival FAQ: Will set times get posted in advance?
content: Yes. During the days leading up to the festival, set times will be posted via this site, our social media sites, the Insomniac app, and email updates (sign up for emails at the bottom of this page) . Set times will also appear on the festival guide you receive upon entry. Note: The lineup is subject to change.

title: Festival FAQ: Can I see a festival map ahead of time?
content: Yes. Maps showing stage locations, food, bathrooms, etc. will be available prior to the event on this site and the Insomniac app.

title: Festival FAQ: Is re-entry allowed?
content: No, ins-and-outs are not allowed (check out Camp EDC Entry for camping in & out policies).

title: Festival FAQ: What is the camera policy?
content: Photo passes are not required for standard cameras with fixed, non-detachable lenses or handheld video devices measuring less than 6 inches. Professional cameras are not permitted. Insomniac does not provide media or photo credentials to independent photographers or videographers.

title: Festival FAQ: Will there be a lost & found?
content: Yes. Lost & Found services will be available at the venue during and between show days. Click for more info on Lost & Found .

title: Festival FAQ: Can I sleep in my car or park overnight?
content: Sleeping in cars in the festival parking lot is not permitted for anyone. DO NOT leave your car in the parking lot during non-festival hours, or it will be towed at your expense. See our Camp EDC guidelines for campground parking rules.

title: Festival FAQ: Does the venue have cash machines?
content: EDC Las Vegas is a cashless event. Credit, debit, Samsung Pay, Apple Pay, and Android Pay will be accepted. Cash can be exchanged onsite for a prepaid card to use with our merchants.

title: Festival FAQ: I’m under 18. Can I attend with a legal guardian?
content: No one under the age of 18 will be allowed into the venue, with or without a guardian.

title: Festival FAQ: What kind of ID do I need?
content: You must present identification to enter the festival and/or buy alcohol. See the complete list of acceptable and unacceptable forms of ID.

title: Festival FAQ: What if my ID is lost or expired?
content: Security will accept expired ID cards ONLY if accompanied by DMV renewal documentation. If your ID was lost or stolen, you must bring a government-issued interim license or passport.

title: Festival FAQ: Can I use a consular ID or foreign driver’s license?
content: Consular IDs are not considered acceptable identification. Foreign government-issued driver’s licenses are acceptable with a photocopy of a passport. A foreign government-issued passport will work on its own.

title: Camp EDC FAQ: Can I buy a single-night camping pass?
content: No, camping passes are not sold on a single-night basis. Only 4-night camping passes are available.

title: Camp EDC FAQ: My friend bought my camping pass for me. How do I pick it up?
content: If you have your friend's camping decal and laminate in hand, you can simply proceed to the venue's camping entrance. If the passes are at Will Call, you must visit our off-site box office before arriving at the venue. You will need to bring the original order number and a photocopy of your friend's credit card and ID to pick up the decal and laminate.

title: Camp EDC FAQ: What security and emergency services will be available?
content: Your safety and well-being is paramount. The campground will be fully staffed by our Ground Control team, as well as medical and security personnel, 24 hours a day.

title: Camp EDC FAQ: Are we allowed to sleep in our cars/oversize vans?
content: No. Sleeping in cars or vans can be a serious health risk due to heat. We do not advise this for anyone!

title: Camp EDC FAQ: Can I grill or cook in the campground?
content: Yes! Small, portable propane stoves/grills are allowed for cooking. Tanks up to 4 lbs (per group) will be allowed into the campground. Please monitor your cooking devices and fully turn off tanks whenever you are not using them. Stay safe, and be aware of your surroundings while cooking. Note: Butane devices, as well as steel knives or other utensils deemed as weapons, will not be allowed into the campground.

title: Camp EDC FAQ: If you confiscate something, can I get it back at the end of the weekend?
content: Prohibited items confiscated at any point—whether at entry or throughout the weekend—will NOT be returned. Please read our list of prohibited items carefully. If you have a question as to whether something is permitted, contact us . If you’re unsure about an item, we advise you to leave it at home.

title: Camp EDC FAQ: Can I purchase an additional parking pass for my campsite?
content: Yes! An Additional Parking Pass allows for members of your group who are arriving separately. The pass costs $95 (plus taxes and fees) and is available as an option when purchasing your Camp EDC pass.

title: Camp EDC FAQ: Will Camp EDC offer RVs for rent?
content: Camp EDC will not offer preset or rental RVs, but we welcome you to drive your own RV on-site! Camp EDC offers a power hookup, RV water refills, and pump-outs for an extra charge. Learn more about RV Camping Passes .

title: Camp EDC FAQ: Can I drive right to my campsite to unload my camping gear?
content: Cars are not permitted to drive into the campground. We are working on a way to provide assistance in moving your gear to your campsite—details to come.

title: FAQs: What are the festival hours?
content: Friday, August 7 - Sunday, August 9 Festival Gates Open - 11:00AM Music Starts - 12:00PM Music Ends - 10:00PM

title: FAQs: Is there a festival map?
content: The Outside Lands festival map can be seen here . The festival map will also be available for viewing on the Outside Lands mobile app .

title: FAQs: What is the bag policy at Outside Lands?
content: While we would prefer that fans come bag free, we realize that is not always possible. Help us to help you enjoy the festival by only bringing the following types and size bags: Backpacks and bags made of clear plastic, clear vinyl, or clear PVC Small bags, fanny-packs, purses up to 6” x 8” x 3” (do not have to be clear) Empty dedicated hydration packs with a bladder capacity of under 2.5L/150 in. and no more than one additional pocket. Standard size backpacks with hydration bladders will not be permitted.

title: FAQs: What items are NOT permitted at the festival?
content: Not Permitted: Non-clear drawstring backpacks Weapons of any kinds (including pocket knives) Illegal substances Glow-sticks (glow bracelets and necklaces are permitted) Alcohol (will be sold at the festival) Glass or cans of ANY kind Video or audio recording equipment (including GoPros - no video recording will be allowed) Professional still camera equipment with a detachable lens longer than 2 inches, tripods, big zooms, or commercial use rigs Skateboards, scooters or personal motorized vehicles Bicycles (not allowed inside festival grounds) Strollers, wagons or carts of any kind Hammocks or slack lines Fireworks, explosives or open flames of any kind Instruments of any kind Laser pointers Umbrellas Selfie sticks of ANY kind, including GoPro sticks Spray paint, large markers or Aerosol cans Picnic baskets Coolers Liquids (excluding personal sized hand sanitizers, which will be permitted) Lawn furniture or any stools or chairs with legs Large inflatables Tents Pets (except service animals) Drones Totems or flags Threatening signs or apparel Native American or “American Indian” headdresses Spiked jewelry or clothing No illegal vending is permitted (no unauthorized or unlicensed vendors are allowed) Any other items deemed unsafe or inappropriate by event or venue management are also prohibited

title: FAQs: Can I leave the festival and return the same day?
content: In general, re-entry is not allowed. You may enter the festival gates once each day. However, if you absolutely must leave the festival for an emergency or serious matter and intend to return the same day, you must speak with a Supervisor at any festival entrance/exit BEFORE LEAVING to be scanned out.

title: Venue: Will there be food at the festival?
content: Outside Lands partners with some of the best restaurants and food trucks the San Francisco Bay Area has to offer. A full list of diverse food vendors on our Taste of the Bay Area can be found HERE . Gluten-free, vegetarian, and vegan options will be available.

title: Venue: Will there be vegan, vegetarian and gluten-free food options?
content: We will have a variety of vendors that will sell vegan, vegetarian and gluten-free food items.

title: Venue: How can I stay hydrated at the festival?
content: There are water refill stations located throughout the festival. Play your part by bringing a reusable container for free refills to stay hydrated all weekend.

title: Venue: Can I stay overnight in the park?
content: Outside Lands is not a camping festival and you cannot sleep in Golden Gate park or your vehicle. No exceptions.

title: Venue: Are strollers allowed?
content: Due to the rough terrain within Golden Gate Park, strollers are NOT permitted at Outside Lands.

title: Venue: Can I bring in my prescription medicine?
content: You may bring in medical prescriptions as long as your name is clearly on the prescription label and you have a valid ID. Names on the prescription must match your valid ID.

title: Venue: Do you have a Lost & Found or Information Booth?
content: Lost & Found is located at the Information Booth on the Polo Field across from Dolores’. Stop by to get your questions answered, check out the festival map, or just to say hi. You can also access our online Lost & Found portal at sfoutsidelands.com/lost .

title: Venue: Cashless Policy
content: Outside Lands is cashless. Credit cards, debit cards, and digital methods of payment are accepted at all points of sale. *Grass Lands (a 21+ area) will still accept cash and will have ATMs.

title: Travel & Transport: PLAN YOUR TRIP
content: There is NO general event parking available at the festival. Please leave your car at home. Parking in the surrounding neighborhoods is reserved for residents and strictly enforced. Attempting to park in surrounding neighborhoods may result in a ticket or tow . See details below on stress-free alternative methods of transportation like the official Outside Lands Shuttle Pass, public transportation (Muni & BART), walking, bikes, scooters and rideshare . Overnight stays in the park or in any vehicles are strictly prohibited. No exceptions .

title: Travel & Transport: I'm traveling from another city, where should I fly in to?
content: San Francisco International Airport (SFO) is approximately 30 minutes from the festival site. Oakland International Airport (OAK) is approximately 50 minutes from the festival site.

title: Travel & Transport: ENTRANCE GATES
content: Line up to enter the festival from the north side at 26th & Fulton to access the North Gate. Line up to enter the festival from the south side at Martin Luther King Jr. & Metson to access the South Gate. Use either 30th or 34th Ave to access Martin Luther King Jr & Metson 31st - 33rd will be closed to all foot traffic and you will not be able to enter on these avenues There is a designated ADA Entrance at 36th Ave & JFK . Review the festival map and note which entrance is best for your ticket type. For GA+ ticket holders: Line up to enter the festival from the north side at 26th & Fulton to access the North Gate. The GA+ expedited entry is on the far left when you arrive at the North Gate. Line up to enter the festival from the south side through the South VIP Gate on Martin Luther King Jr Drive (just west of the South Gate). For VIP & Golden Gate Club ticket holders: The VIP Entrance is located on the north side at 36th Ave & JFK Drive featuring a dedicated lane exclusively for Golden Gate Club members. If you are taking the official Outside Lands Shuttle, for your convenience, there is a VIP Entrance on the south side located on Martin Luther King Jr Drive, west of the South Gate.

title: Travel & Transport: BART
content: BART will run service in the Millbrae direction until approximately 1AM and in East Bay directions until approximately 12:30AM on Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Plan your trip using the BART Trip Planner . BART Parking is free after 3PM on Friday and is free on Saturday and Sunday except for the Milpitas and Berryessa/North San Jose stations, which are not operated by BART. BART now accepts credit card “Tap and Ride” payments making it even easier for you to ride. For more information, visit their website here .

title: Travel & Transport: MUNI
content: Muni continues to be a great way to get to and from Outside Lands from all over the city. Muni is providing extra service to ensure festival ticket holders have more ways to get to and from Golden Gate Park: Pre-event (outbound to the park): Take 5 Fulton or 5R Fulton Rapid buses from downtown to Fulton & 30th Ave. We will also run extra N Judah trains along all of the line’s normal stops. Post-event (inbound to downtown): There will be a special 5X Civic Center Express buses that will take you directly from Fulton & 30th back to Civic Center/UN Plaza BART. We will also continue to run extra N Judah trains at all normal stops. Have questions about how to get to and from Outside Lands via Muni? Visit SFMTA’s Outside Lands page for everything you need to know. Never taken Muni before? Check this quick start guide . Plan your Muni trip on 511.org or Google Maps . If you experience or witness an incident, help make Muni a safe space for all by reporting it using the Muni Feedback form at SFMTA.com/MuniFeedback , the 311 mobile app or by calling 311. Non-English speakers should call 311 for language assisted reporting. Muni Map Muni Routes

title: Travel & Transport: BIKE
content: Outside Lands offers free self-park bicycle parking during festival hours in designated areas located along the east and south sides of the festival. Need a bike to ride to Outside Lands? Lyft Bikes has you covered with special stations on the north and south sides of the festival. On-site valets will make sure there’s an open dock for you to park when you roll up to the festival, and a bike when you’re ready to head home. Designated Lyft Bike station locations: JFK Drive, just east of Transverse Drive, near the North Gate festival entrance Martin Luther King Jr Drive, just east of the South Gate festival entrance

title: Travel & Transport: SCOOTER
content: Grab a Lime scooter for an easy ride to the festival. Just download the Lime app, create your account and find a nearby vehicle on the map. When you’re ready to ride, scan the QR code to unlock and go. Use code OSL30 to save 30% off 2 Lime rides* during Outside Lands 2026. *See full Terms and Conditions in-app. While supplies last. Know before you roll: Open the app to map routes & find nearby rides Stick to bike lanes & park in designated zones Rolling with friends? Share the code so your whole crew saves Designated Lime parking locations: Entering from the north side? Park along JFK Drive, just east of Transverse Drive, near the North Gate . Entering from the south side? Park along Martin Luther King Jr Drive, east of the South Gate .

title: Travel & Transport: WALK
content: San Francisco is a walkable city! Walking is a great way to get to the festival. Refer to the Entrance Gates section above for information on the best gates to route to if you’re arriving on foot.

title: Travel & Transport: DRIVE
content: There is NO general event parking available at the festival. Please leave your car at home. Parking in the surrounding neighborhoods is reserved for residents and strictly enforced. Attempting to park in surrounding neighborhoods may result in a ticket or tow. Take alternative methods of transportation.

title: Travel & Transport: RIDESHARE
content: Lyft is the official rideshare partner of Outside Lands. New to Lyft? Download the app & use code OSL26 to get 50% off your first two rides (max $10/ride). *Subject to Lyft terms. Request your ride to and from the official rideshare pick-up/drop-off locations below to avoid any issues: Balboa & 30th Ave (adjacent to George Washington High School) Irving St. between 25th and 27th Avenue

title: Travel & Transport: DROP OFFS
content: If you’re planning on getting dropped off at Outside Lands, please know that some streets will be congested or closed entirely to traffic. You can expect nearby streets to be especially congested before and after the event. For this reason, we suggest you get dropped off several blocks north or south of the park. We recommend Geary Blvd or Balboa St to the north, or Irving Street to the south. Official rideshare pick-up and drop-off locations are: Balboa & 30th Avenue (adjacent to George Washington High School) Irving St. between 25th and 27th Avenue Requesting your ride to and from these locations will help you avoid any issues. The SFMTA’s Slow Streets program is designed to limit through traffic on certain residential streets and allow them to be used as a shared space for people traveling by foot and by bicycle. There are several slow streets in the immediate area, which will further impact vehicular traffic.

title: Health & Safety: Is there a medical staff on-site at Outside Lands?
content: Rock Medicine will be on-site to help you with any type of medical problem. Rock Medicine has been providing free medical care at concerts and festivals since 1973. If you need medical assistance, please alert a staff member.

title: Health & Safety: What should I do if I have a security issue or witness an emergency situation?
content: Event staff, security personnel and law enforcement will be located throughout the site for the duration of the event to create a safe and secure environment for all festival attendees. If you have an EMERGENCY, find a staff member with a radio or go to the closest information, medical tent, or entrance gate for assistance. Be ready to convey the nature and details of the incident.

title: Health & Safety: How do I find an emergency exit?
content: Emergency exit and evacuation route signs are posted throughout the festival. Please remember to familiarize yourself with your nearest exit as you move around the festival site. In case of emergency, listen to instructions and follow directions posted on the stage screens.

title: Health & Safety: How do I register for emergency alerts impacting Outside Lands?
content: Text OUTSIDELANDS to 888-777 to register for emergency alerts impacting Outside Lands

title: Festival Accessibility
content: We strive to make Golden Gate Park as ADA-friendly as possible, including handicap parking, raised viewing areas, and wheelchair-friendly walkways. For more information or festival weekend related requests, please see our accessibility page or email access@sfoutsidelands.com . If you are requesting a Sign Language interpreter, please make your requests at least 30 days in advance of the festival dates to ensure availability and to allow for adequate preparation. We will attempt to arrange an interpreter on shorter notice, but cannot guarantee availability.
